open_issues: Known coverage change: checkpoint_write_failure_keeps_verdict (attribution.rs) and check_attribution_push_failure_keeps_the_verdict (cli tests/binary.rs) set a pushurl to a missing path. They are now refused by the guard instead of failing in git. The workspace run excluding athena-core passed both. The athena-git hook test keeps git's own push failure covered.

Behavior change: `athena land --pr` now refuses ssh and scp-style GitHub origins that parse_remote used to accept, and any origin with a second or mismatched push or fetch URL. The CHANGELOG line says so.
Strict comparison of fetch and push URLs fails closed: a path-case difference, or an explicit port on one URL only, is refused.
mistakes: My hook test first used std::fs::set_permissions, which the workspace test no_in_process_exec_writes rejects. I replaced it with athena_testkit::write_executable.
I did not re-run xtask policy or the whole workspace after that last test-only edit.
learnings: `git remote get-url --push --all origin` falls back to the fetch URLs, so one pair of reads covers both. Two `git config --add remote.origin.pushurl` calls make a real double.
Git does not hand the pusher's `-c core.hooksPath` to a local receive-pack, so a pre-receive hook in a bare repo still runs under Git::isolated.
athena-testkit's no_in_process_exec_writes test refuses set_permissions in test code; tests that need an executable must use athena_testkit::write_executable.
`mod remote` in gh is private but reachable from sibling and child modules, so gh/mod.rs did not need an edit.
